notes:
Summary:
- Mid-market CX SaaS (customer support automation + knowledge search).
- Started on Redwood Hosted API (Q4 2025) for quick chat + rerank proofs; positive perf vs incumbents.
- Evaluating Dedicated for predictable latency, throughput and data isolation.

POC / Technical timeline:
- 2025-12-08: Sandbox onboarding, hosted API keys issued. small pilot (10 agents).
- 2026-01-12: Hosted API perf baseline collected (median latency 220ms for short chat flows).
- 2026-02-20: Dedicated demo (Avery / Carlos / infra). Showed autoscaling, canary rollouts, KV prefix cache.
- 2026-02-25: 14-day Dedicated POC kickoff; target throughput = 600 reqs/min (chat + rerank mix), 95th pct token latency goal < 250ms.
- 2026-03-04: POC mid-check: throughput steady, cost estimates trending ~20% above internal target without quantization. SE suggested mixed precision + smaller model routing for low-critical flows.

Business requirements / priorities:
- Primary: predictable latency and single-tenant isolation for customer PII paths.
- Must support Okta SSO for admin console and SAML for audit.
- Need KMS integration for encryption keys; prefer customer-managed CMEK for prod models.
- Data residency: EU region for EU customers (DPA redline).
- Rollout: start with 5% of production traffic on Dedicated; automatic fallback to Hosted API in failover.

Procurement / Legal conversation notes:
- Legal reviewed Redwood MSA v1 on 2026-02-28. Major redlines returned 2026-03-02.
  - Indemnity: Harborline requested carveouts for customer data processing; Redwood proposed mutual indemnity with limitation.
  - Liability cap: Harborline wants higher cap tied to net fees; Redwood offered standard 12 months of fees.
  - SLA: Harborline asked for 99.9% tiered SLO for Dedicated instances + credits; Redwood provided draft SLA but Harborline wants explicit latency targets (95th token latency) and escalation path.
  - DPA: require EU data residency clause and subprocessors list. Harborline legal flagged retention windows and deletion certificate.
- Pricing: negotiating Dedicated reserved capacity (3-node baseline + burst). Harborline prefers 12-month commit with option to scale at quarter boundaries. Pricing sheet v3 in Drive.
- Procurement team requires vendor onboarding questionnaire (security questionnaire 80% complete). SOC2 Type II report provided by Redwood; legal has copy in drive.

Open action items / next steps:
- AE (Avery) to deliver revised MSA redline tracker with comments by 2026-03-08.
- SE (Carlos) to produce statement-of-work-like POC addendum describing baseline config and failover within 48h.
- Procurement to confirm POC-to-production acceptance criteria (throughput/latency/cost) and finalize ARR band.
- Security to finish vendor onboarding (remaining: penetration test report and pen-test remediation plan).
- Schedule final legal negotiation call: proposed 2026-03-10 (30-45m) — invite: Avery, Carlos, Maya, Harborline GC, Redwood legal lead.

CRM-style notes / snippets from calls:
- "Hosted perf was good, but dedicated isolation is non-negotiable for enterprise customers" — Harborline CTO (02/20 demo).
- "Need concrete latency numbers in SLA; can't accept fuzzy uptime only" — Procurement lead (03/02).
- "If we can get CMEK + EU residency and a reasonable liability cap we're ready to sign a 12-month commit" — Head of Ops (03/04).

Risk and negotiation posture:
- Risk: DPA redlines and liability cap could push to a managed-host competitor who accepts broader liability.
- Opp: Harborline is product-led and will promote Redwood in their partner ecosystem if integration goes smoothly — helpful for reference and co-marketing.
